text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-84217 runtime.latency.p95 > 3500ms in us-west-2 (service: inference-runtime)
pagerduty: Incident PD-84217 created and routed to oncall (sophie).
sophie: ack oncall — I'm on it, grabbing logs and dashboards. @darren FYI since this smells like infra/network.
sophie: quick look at console: spike started ~3071234500, p95 up to 4s, p50 fine. Traffic looks steady.
darren: thanks. checking node health and GPU load. running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep serving` now.
darren: found 2 pods in ServingPool-7 showing high restart_count 1 but Ready=1. pulling systemd/journal for those nodes.
mike: I'm watching the routing layer — rate limiter rollout yesterday might be interacting with batching. can we confirm if batching config changed?
sophie: no rollout in last 24h from our deploy dashboard. last config change 2 days ago.
elaine: PD note: customers flagged 3 slow calls in last 10m, no widespread errors reported.
sophie: ok, first mitigation: scale up serving-pool by +2 nodes to reduce queue depth. doing `terraform apply` standby autoscale.
darren: also clearing local prefix cache on the two noisy pods to rule out a KV-cache stall. command: 
```
kubectl exec -n inference servingpool-7-aaa -- /bin/sh -c "rm -rf /var/cache/kv && service inference restart"
```
sophie: executed scale and cache clear. monitoring.
mike: I toggled the rate limiter to permissive for canary route for 2m to see if latency drops. will watch for increased errors.
darren: I see latency drop in tail for one pod already — p95 from 4s -> 1.2s on that instance.
sophie: nice. PD: I'm marking as acknowledged and annotating mitigations.
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PD-84217 acknowledged by sophie.
elaine: customer impact assessment: 3 customers affected, short lived, no data loss, not a legal/regulatory impact. recommend no-wide-notify.
mike: digging into logs — a hot shard on KV backend caused one pod to fall behind on async writes, causing local request queuing. KV backend shows spike at 3071234470.
darren: we put a temporary circuit on that KV proxy to fail fast if latency > 800ms. patch applied.
sophie: observing 8m after mitigation p95 stabilized ~380ms across pool, p50 80ms. stitching these metrics to the PD incident notes.
incident-bot: PD-84217 auto-resolved (no active alerts) at 3071234580.
pagerduty: PD-84217 resolved by incident-bot.
mike: leaving a short postmortem draft in #postmortems/inference: root cause KV hot shard, contributing factor: recent rate limiter config + uneven KV routing. action items: (1) KV shard rebalancing, (2) add circuit-breaker metric to alerting, (3) add synthetic traffic test for KV backpressure.
sophie: good list. I'll create follow-ups and assign. @elaine please help with customer comms draft saying brief latency blip, limited customers affected, mitigations taken.
elaine: will draft and share here in 30m.
sophie: handing off to next oncall @mike for overnight watch — I'll update rotation.
mike: ack, I'll keep an eye for 2h. ping me if it recurs. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: from sophie to mike at 3071234595.
pagerduty: PD-84217 closed in PagerDuty.
sophie: thanks team, nice quick loop.
